title: FOX, NBC, get two of ex-ESPN games at center of NFL media rights talks
article_text:
The NFL is indeed set for additional broadcast television inventory this coming season, with FOX and NBC receiving some of the ex-ESPN inventory that at one point was earmarked for YouTube.

The NFL awarded FOX and NBC one game each out of the four windows ESPN relinquished as part of its deal to acquire NFL Network, Sports Media Watch has learned. The league is also expected to convert one regionally distributed game each on FOX and CBS to a national window.

The end result will be four additional national windows on broadcast television using a mix of new and existing inventory.

The league had been expected to see a slight increase in broadcast television inventory this season, and the ex-ESPN windows will functionally shift cable-exclusive inventory to broadcast. (Officially, the four ex-ESPN windows contractually belonged to ABC and ESPN+ as part of overlapping “Monday Night Football” doubleheaders. But with ABC apparently set to simulcast ESPN games in those four weeks instead, the change amounts to dropping four ESPN-exclusive editions of “MNF.”)

Fox CEO Lachlan Murdoch said on an earnings call Monday that the company’s new windows would consist of a Week 10 International Series game from Munich, which would air in an early morning window as part of a FOX tripleheader — the first NFL tripleheader on a single broadcast network since 2016. The second would be a Saturday game in Week 15. It was not clear which game came out of the ex-ESPN inventory and which was elevated from the Fox regional slate.

NBC announced Monday that its additional inventory would be a Saturday game in Week 17 leading into its annual Peacock-exclusive game, giving the company three exclusive windows that week.

CBS announced later Monday that its additional game window will air on primetime on the Saturday of Week 15, creating a split-network doubleheader with Fox on December 19. That is likely to be the day on which the College Football Playoff schedules the bulk of its first round games.

The additional broadcast TV inventory comes as the NFL faces a federal investigation into its rights deals with streaming companies that has been cheerled — and potentially may have even been sparked — by Fox Corporation.

The four ex-ESPN windows were originally expected to form the bulk of a new five-game media rights package — also including the league’s new International Series game from Australia — that the league had been reportedly shopping throughout the offseason. At some point in the process, the NFL is said to have shifted from shopping a single five-game package to splitting that inventory between Netflix and Google-owned YouTube. John Ourand of Puck reported last week that YouTube was not interested in that arrangement, and the two games it would have received were instead shopped to broadcast television.

The other two games are expected to go to Netflix, which would presumably form a ‘five-game package’ featuring those two contests, the Australia game, and its existing Christmas Day inventory.

title: Fifa power struggle: Uefa backs Diallo but is battle to unseat Infantino a lost cause?
article_text:
Uefa finally has a credible challenger to Gianni Infantino after Philippe Diallo, the head of the French Football Federation (FFF), confirmed he will run for the Fifa presidency.

The deadline for candidates to declare will pass on Wednesday, and it looked as though Infantino would escape serious opposition after Uefa failed to persuade former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger to stand against him.

Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin had initially urged his close ally Nasser Al Khelaifi, the chairman of Paris Saint-Germain, to run for the position, and while the Qatari declined, he is said to have played a key role in securing Diallo's candidacy. The question really, though, is whether anyone can pose a serious threat to the entrenched incumbent?

Uefa has long wanted to topple Infantino, who was blocked in his bid to sell off 25 per cent of the World Cup after the 2026 tournament in North America. Infantino was left fighting for his job after he attempted to seal a deal with Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital that would also have seen him secure a highly paid commissioner's role.

That followed a scandal-ridden summer for Infantino, including the Folarin Balogun affair, where Fifa overturned the US player's suspension following a personal request from President Donald Trump.

Germany's national team coach, Jurgen Klopp, this week became the latest high-profile figure to demand Infantino's exit.

“I've been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am, but I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense,” said former Liverpool boss Klopp.

“I didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that.”

“Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job,” Klopp added.

Uefa will hope that person is Diallo. The vote for Fifa's next president will take place in March 2027 at its annual congress in Morocco.

Diallo has been head of the FFF since 2023. The 63-year-old was re-elected in December 2024 for a four-year term.

In September, the FFF withdrew its support for Infantino, with Diallo saying that “the trust placed in the Fifa president has been broken”, adding that France's decision formed part of a broader movement within Uefa.

Born in Saint-Nazaire in 1963, Diallo pursued a career as a player, progressing through the youth ranks at Nantes.

After studying law and graduating from Sciences Po in Paris, Diallo moved into sports administration. In 1992, he became involved with the Union of Professional Football Clubs (UCPF). He went on to serve as its chief executive for almost three decades.

He also joined the board of the French Professional League in 2009 and became involved in international governance, serving on Fifa's Dispute Resolution Chamber. Diallo joined the FFF's executive committee in March 2021, initially as treasurer, before becoming president.

It is felt that Diallo – whose father was a Senegalese boxing champion and represented France in the 1960 Olympics – is a respected figure and could enjoy support in parts of Africa and beyond.

Earlier in November, Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima announced his intention to run for Fifa's top position, but the 68-year-old is expected to be an outsider.

Last month, former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega was the first candidate to publicly declare his intention to challenge his fellow Swiss, Infantino.

Candidates require the backing of five national associations to stand in the election.

A simple majority of 106 votes is needed at Fifa's Congress and, as things stand, Infantino appears to have the numbers.

When the scandal erupted in late July, Infantino knew he was in trouble and followed a grovelling apology by hunkering down to ride out the storm.

Uefa talked boycotts, criminal cases, and there were even leaked stories about Infantino's personal life. But, as is the case with all political scandals, momentum is key, and Uefa let it slip.

Infantino regained his confidence – and his passport – and has been doing what he does best: travelling around the world in his private jet, wooing member federations.

The Financial Times reported that Infantino has visited more than 30 countries since August, with promises of increased Fifa funding should he be re-elected. That included a quick stop in the Philippines to pledge an extra $20m to rebuild a stadium in Manila.

Even by his own standards, Infantino has been incredibly nomadic – Bhutan, Bangladesh, Aruba, Mongolia … the list goes on – as he seeks to make the most of Fifa's one-federation, one-vote system. In Fifa, the likes of England, France, Germany and Brazil have the same voting power as Montserrat, its smallest member.

Infantino enjoys the support of Africa (CAF) and Asia (AFC), with both blocs now publicly backing him. That gives the 56-year-old 100 votes and leaves him on the brink of another term, particularly given that the 10 votes of South America's Conmebol usually go his way, and he enjoys considerable support in the Caribbean.

Uefa will hope that a serious individual like Diallo can persuade federations to defect from the current regime. There is a fear, though, that he lacks the heft of Al Khelaifi or the prestige of Wenger.

The FFF chief should bank the majority of Uefa's 55 votes, but it is clear that serious work must be done to oust Infantino, who has spent the past decade ingratiating himself with many of the world's smaller and more remote federations, whose members might be less perturbed by his many scandals.

title: Disney+ bolsters ESPN portfolio in Spain with WOW FC MMA rights
article_text:
US media giant Disney’s Disney+ OTT streaming service has expanded its sports rights portfolio in Spain, adding domestic mixed martial arts (MMA) promotion Way of Warriors FC (WOW FC).

Through the ‘exclusive’ domestic right agreement, Disney+ will broadcast live WOW FC fight nights live and on demand, alongside ancillary content and shoulder programming, on the ESPN-branded content area of its platform, at no extra cost to subscribers.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

This deal will begin with the upcoming WOW 34 event at Valencia’s 15,600-capacity Roig Arena on November 21.

Speaking on the announcement, Disney+ country manager for Spain Simon Anselm said: “The arrival of WOW FC on ESPN on Disney+ reinforces our commitment to offering our customers new forms of entertainment.

“MMA combines competition, excitement and spectacle, and this agreement allows us to bring the experience of its live fight nights to a broader audience, while also bringing them closer to the stories behind its fighters.”

Ilia Topuria, a two-time champion in the major UFC promotion and a partner in WOW FC, added: “Disney+, through ESPN, has played a major role in the growth and global expansion of MMA, helping to turn our sport into a global phenomenon.

“This agreement represents much more than a distribution agreement: it is a historic step for MMA in Spain and an extraordinary opportunity for our athletes to inspire millions of people. I am convinced that together we are going to build something truly special.”

This follows the recent launch of ESPN as a content area on Disney+ to select markets across Europe, positioning the sports broadcasting brand as Disney’s key consumer sports arm.

In Spain in particular, the platform holds the rights to UEFA Women's Champions League soccer, Formula E motor racing, NHL ice hockey, and more.

The wider lineup also features college sports such as the NCAA men's and women's basketball tournaments (March Madness), college football playoffs, and bowl games, as well as other sports rights in select markets, most recent of those being the NHL, and NBA basketball in 11 European markets, including neighboring Portugal.

title: DAZN adds WatchAFL, WatchNRL to global sports offering
article_text:
Global sports OTT platform DAZN has announced a deal to carry WatchAFL and WatchNRL, the international streaming services for the Australian Football League (AFL) and National Rugby League (NRL), respectively.

Through the agreements, the men’s AFL and the women’s AFLW competitions and the NRL and NRLW will be available across DAZN’s 200 markets.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

WatchAFL and WatchNRL were previously operated by Foxtel Group, which holds Australian broadcast and streaming rights to both properties and is part of DAZN’s global platform following its acquisition of Foxtel in April 2025.

International viewers will have access to every match of the 2027 AFL Premiership Season and Finals Series, alongside the AFLW, AFL Origin, the AAMI Community Series, select classic matches, and AFL news and entertainment programming.

The launch on DAZN comes ahead of the 2026 AFLW Grand Final, which takes place on November 27.

The 2027 AFL Origin match will see Western Australia take on South Australia at Optus Stadium in Perth on 27 February, ahead of the AFL Premiership Season commencing in mid-March, with the opening round featuring all 18 clubs in a traditional nine-game round of football fixtures across the country.

Meanwhile, WatchNRL will provide coverage of the 2027 NRL Premiership, including the Finals and pre-season, alongside the State of Origin Series, the NRL Women’s Premiership, select classic matches and news and entertainment programming from Fox League.

The 2027 Premiership season kicks off at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on February 27 (local time), with Melbourne Storm taking on Wests Tigers and Parramatta Eels facing Gold Coast Titans.

The AFL and NRL’s OTT offerings join DAZN’s portfolio of global sports and competitions, including FIFA+, NFL Game Pass, NHL.TV, Courtside 1891 (FIBA basketball) and Rally TV.

Andrew Dillon, AFL CEO, said: “The passion for Australian football extends well beyond Australia. Bringing WatchAFL onto DAZN’s global platform makes that connection easier, while also giving both the AFL and AFLW an even greater opportunity to reach new audiences and introduce our game to sports fans around the world.

“We’re incredibly proud of our game and ambitious about its international reach. This partnership is another important step in taking Australian football to more people in more places.”

Peter V’landys AM, executive chairman of the Australian Rugby League Commission, added: “Rugby League is made for the world stage. The pace and physicality of the game and the passion of our fans resonate wherever it's seen, and WatchNRL’s launch on DAZN gives us a brilliant new platform to showcase that to fans globally.

“We want to grow rugby league, reach new audiences, and ensure the game is accessible to more fans than ever before. Placing WatchNRL alongside some of the world’s biggest sporting competitions gives us the platform to achieve that.”

title: Betano announces suspension of master sponsorship deal with Flamengo
RBC City National Bank renews Golden Knights sponsorship for 10 years
article_text:
RBC City National Bank has signed a 10-year renewal of its founding sponsorship of the Golden Knights that preserves its entitlement rights to the team’s practice facility through 2037 and expands its marketing rights across the Foley Entertainment Group portfolio. The L.A.-based subsidiary of Royal Bank of Canada became the NHL franchise’s official bank before its on-ice debut in 2017.

Financial terms were not disclosed, but Golden Knights President of Business Operations John Penhollow called the agreement the team’s most lucrative corporate partnership. The practice-facility entitlement represents particularly valuable inventory for the Golden Knights, who do not control the naming rights to their home venue, T-Mobile Arena, under their minority ownership agreement. Penhollow said he believes the City National agreement is the NHL’s most valuable practice-facility entitlement deal and one of its most valuable team-level sponsorships overall.

The core assets in the original deal remain in place, including naming rights to City National Arena, branding at the practice facility and T-Mobile Arena and an annual title night at a Golden Knights game. The renewal, however, significantly expands the bank’s rights across other properties in Golden Knights owner Bill Foley’s portfolio.

City National will have a larger presence in the Las Vegas sports market through the Foley-owned AHL Henderson Silver Knights, IFL Vegas Knight Hawks and Lee’s Family Forum. The partnership will also allow City National to tap into Foley’s hotels, wineries and destination properties and expand its relationship with Premier League club AFC Bournemouth.

Selling sponsors on the breadth of the FEG portfolio, which includes sports and luxury hospitality properties, has been an organizational priority since Penhollow took the reins in June 2025.

“For some brands, like RBC City National Bank, they have an interest in really engaging with all of the above,” Penhollow said. “That’s not for everybody, but this is one particular relationship where they saw the value in going to all these different entities and engaging with our fans, engaging with our athletes, engaging with the community in each of these areas.”

The expansion comes as City National, a bank with longstanding ties to the entertainment industry, seeks to grow its sports business. RBC U.S. Chief Strategy Officer Tyler Friedman said the firm has made a strategic push into corporate sports banking over the past 18 months, including hiring Anthony Di Santi to lead its dedicated practice.

“This partnership is accretive to that strategic move that we’re making into corporate sports,” Friedman said. “Between the history of City National and entertainment, which includes sports, where the market is driving eyeballs, and our strategic push into a corporate sports segment, all of that has sort of made this partnership a valuable and important one for City National.”

The Golden Knights and City National negotiated the deal directly without agency involvement. In addition to Penhollow, who oversees Foley’s Nevada-based properties, AFC Bournemouth President & co-CEO Jim Frevola, Golden Knights COO Rich Wang and Golden Knights VP/Global Partnerships Glenn Israelsky contributed to the renewal negotiations with City National.

title: ESPN gets at least 91 of Major League Volleyball's 140 matches in 2027
article_text:
Major League Volleyball's 2027 media deal spreads a record 140 matches across four partners, and ESPN carries at least 91. Scripps Sports has 15 Friday primetime matches.

This story was produced through MarketScale. See how Sports & Entertainment teams put it to work with Events & Onsite Capture.

Thursday nights go to Peacock. Friday nights go to Scripps Sports and ION. Weekends go to ESPN. That's how Major League Volleyball's 2027 media lineup, announced November 17, lays out a league-record 140 matches across four partners. Sports Video Group reported that NBC Sports and ESPN are new to the league, and Scripps Sports/ION and CBS Sports are coming back.

The 140 is the headline number, but where those matches land matters more. For a brand weighing a women's volleyball buy, or a league executive studying how a fourth-year property built a national footprint, the split across partners is what to read first.

In its own release, the league says it designed the schedule around a steady weekly rhythm, with set nights of volleyball on each platform. The league's viewing guide spells out what a fan needs for each window, and that's the detail an ad buyer should care about:

- NBC Sports: each Thursday for 16 weeks, Peacock streams a weekly MLV Match of the Week, available with Peacock Premium or a higher tier. On April 11, 2027, one match moves to the NBC broadcast network: the new Minnesota Forge host the defending champion Dallas Pulse.

- Scripps Sports and ION: 18 matches, 15 of them in Friday primetime. They start on the free Scripps Sports Network and move to ION after All-Star weekend. ION is again the exclusive home of Championship Weekend, both semifinals and the final.

- ESPN: at least 91 matches on weekends and other weeknights across ESPN networks. Matches also stream on Disney+ in select international countries, and the MLV Draft airs November 23 at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN+.

- CBS Sports: the All-Star Match on March 27 on CBS, also streaming on Paramount+, plus 10 matches on CBS Sports Network.

Set nights are something a media planner can actually plan around. Sixteen straight Thursdays on one platform works like a recurring placement, a time slot a sponsor can build a season of creative for. It's a different buy from a handful of big one-off events. ESPN's release, from its press room, describes the deal as putting MLV next to the network's wider women's sports programming. Partners also get distinct roles: Peacock gets a weekly franchise and Scripps owns Friday.

CBS is the continuity in the lineup. In the league's release, Billy Stone of CBS Sports noted that his network has worked with Major League Volleyball from the league's very start. Jon Miller of NBC Sports described the network's arrival as a way to put more of volleyball's biggest moments in front of fans nationwide, which fits a package built around one broadcast-network date and a weekly streaming slot.

The cost of entry also changes by night. According to the viewing guide, Scripps Sports Network costs nothing on FAST platforms such as Tubi, Samsung TV Plus, Amazon Prime, Fire TV and Google TV. ESPN's matches sit in the ESPN App, which viewers reach with a subscription or through certain pay TV packages, and a Disney+, Hulu and ESPN bundle is also available. Compared with Peacock's Premium requirement, that makes Friday the league's free entry point and turns the rest of the week into a series of subscription decisions.

ESPN networks carry at least 91 of the 140 matches, mostly on weekends and other weeknights. The over-the-air windows sit elsewhere: Scripps Sports carries 18 matches, including 15 on Friday nights in primetime, plus the April 11 NBC match and the All-Star Match on CBS. Peacock has a Thursday Match of the Week for 16 weeks, and CBS Sports Network carries 10 matches.

ION gives the package wide reach. The league's viewing guide says ION reaches more than 128 million homes, delivered over the air and via cable, satellite and streaming platforms.

This is our read, not something the league has said: for a sponsor whose brief is awareness, the Friday block and the two broadcast-network dates are where most new viewers are likely to find the sport. For a sponsor that wants to reach the same engaged fan over and over, ESPN's volume and Peacock's weekly run make more sense. The strongest objection is that the split looks sharper on paper than in a real living room. A household with a pay TV package can get most of it, and the announcement doesn't say how ESPN's 91 matches divide between linear channels and ESPN+.

Sports Business Journal's account adds a wrinkle: it puts the at-least-91 matches on ESPN+ via the ESPN App, where the league and ESPN releases say "ESPN networks." For a buyer, that wording is the difference between a streaming audience and a linear one, so it's the first line item worth checking against the full schedule.

Scripps already had a history with the league. Maria Kholodova reported in SportBusiness on March 24, 2026, that a 12-game MLV package was part of the lineup when Scripps Sports Network launched as a free ad-supported television (FAST) channel. Under the 2027 deal, coverage shifts to ION once All-Star weekend is over. In the league's release, Scripps Sports president Brian Lawlor said the company took pride in the part its MLV partnership this past season played in the rising worldwide popularity of volleyball.

title: Tour de France widens sponsorship gap over Giro and Vuelta, says GlobalData
article_text:
The Tour de France has cemented its commercial dominance over cycling’s other two Grand Tours in 2026, leading on sponsorship value, media reach and prize money, according to GlobalData.

The firm’s report, “Post-Event Analysis – Cycling Grand Tours 2026”, found that the Giro d’Italia signed the highest number of partners and the Vuelta a España leaned on its shared organiser ASO, but neither matched the Tour’s long-term commercial power.

Value at the Tour is concentrated among a small group of jersey and main partners. LCL, E.Leclerc, Skoda, Krys, Continental and Groupama together account for more than half of the race’s sponsorship value.

Olivia Snooks, sport analyst at GlobalData, said: “The Tour de France remains cycling’s most valuable property by some distance. Its jersey sponsors are mostly French brands buying national visibility, and media contracts running to 2030 give ASO a secure revenue base. Even with live UK coverage moving behind a paywall for the first time in four decades, TNT Sports reported strong audience growth, which shows how much demand the race commands.”

The Tour also has the broadest media footprint of the three races. Free-to-air television remains the backbone of both the Tour and the Vuelta, reflecting ASO’s preference for public service broadcasters that maximise reach for sponsors. As ASO organises the Tour and co-organises the Vuelta, the two races share most of their broadcasters, with most media deals secured to the end of the decade.

The Giro, organised by RCS Sport, sells its rights separately and relies more on pay-TV. It has confirmed long-term terms for only one of its media deals, with Warner Bros. Discovery.

Snooks said: “The Giro sells volume and destinations. It has the largest sponsor roster of the three races, but regional governments and tourism bodies, from Friuli Venezia Giulia to Abruzzo and Valle d’Aosta, fund almost a third of its sponsorship value as they pay to host stages and promote themselves.

“The Bulgarian Grande Partenza delivered record audiences for Eurosport and HBO Max, but since Enel’s long-running deal ended, the maglia rosa has relied on stopgap sponsors. Securing a long-term anchor partner remains the Giro’s main commercial gap.”

The Vuelta has the smallest sponsorship portfolio of the three and no dominant partner. Title sponsor Carrefour leads a roster built mostly on modest deals with Spanish brands.

Prize money follows the same hierarchy: Tadej Pogačar’s winner’s prize at the Tour was nearly double what Jonas Vingegaard earned for winning the Giro, and more than three times Enric Mas’ prize for winning the Vuelta.

Snooks added: “Pogačar and Vingegaard shaped the 2026 season. One won the Giro, the other the Tour, and both crashed out of another Grand Tour. The drop in online engagement at the Vuelta after Pogačar’s exit shows both the value and the risk of relying on a few headline names. For the Vuelta, larger stand-alone Spanish and international partnerships would help narrow the gap with its two bigger rivals, rather than relying on agreements shared with the Tour.”

title: Several sports stars back Matchwornshirt in £15.5m investment round
article_text:
MatchWornShirt (MWS), the international online memorabilia auction platform, has secured another £15.5 million ($20.4 million) in investment, with backing from several athletes.

A range of investors from across the sporting world have teamed up with the company, including Gamma Waves Partners (the global investor founded by Italian soccer's Giorgio Chiellini and Andrea Agnelli).

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Further investment has come from the ownership group behind the Indiana Pacers and Indiana Fever, Joyned Capital (which counts Premier League soccer star Jurrien Timber as a member), and 35V (the investment vehicle for NBA superstar Kevin Durant and his business partner Rich Kleiman).

Individuals including English soccer legend John Terry are also involved in the funding.

Tijmen Zonderwijk, co-founder and chief executive at MWS, commented: "The scale of the names and businesses involved in this group of investors demonstrates a collective passion for what we have already built here at MWS, and for that, we’re incredibly proud."

Founded nine years ago, Netherlands-based MWS counts top-tier soccer clubs such as Chelsea, AC Milan, and Paris Saint-Germain amongst its partners.

In terms of activity this year, meanwhile, March saw the firm agree a deal in the US with top-flight competition Major League Soccer (MLS) and its players' association (MLSPA).

Kyang Yung, Gamma Waves Partners' chief investment officer, added: "In evaluating this investment, we found a rare combination of category leadership, a fast-growing collector base, and significant room to expand across many sports and categories. We are proud to support MWS in its next phase of growth as lead investor.”

title: Scottish Rugby extends two partnership agreements
article_text:
Saltire Energy has agreed a three-year extension to a relationship that began in 2021. The Aberdeen-based company will continue to support Scotland Men’s international matchdays alongside two grassroots programmes, the Saltire Energy Rugby Schools Week and Saltire Energy Caledonia Cup.

The Schools Week programme has engaged more than 70,000 pupils at over 600 state schools since its launch in 2021 and forms part of Scottish Rugby’s State School Strategy. The Saltire Energy Caledonia Cup also brought together more than 600 young players for its regional Finals Day in March.

Alongside that agreement, Highland Spring has extended its exclusive relationship with Scottish Rugby for a further two years and will remain Official Water Supplier until at least 2028.

Since the partnership began in 2024, Highland Spring has supplied more than 90,000 litres of water to Scotland’s men’s, women’s and U20 teams, as well as Glasgow Warriors and Edinburgh Rugby.

The next phase of the partnership will include increased on-field visibility, further content around hydration and a coaching session or community day at a local rugby club involving a former Scotland player. Highland Spring products will also remain available at Scottish Gas Murrayfield, alongside a recycling programme for empty bottles.

The partnership generated 5.4 million social and digital impressions across its first two seasons, according to Scottish Rugby, while television exposure reached 9.56 million during 2025/26.

Together, the two renewals extend support across both elite and grassroots rugby in Scotland. While Saltire Energy will continue its involvement with international matchdays and youth participation, Highland Spring will retain a role spanning Scotland’s national teams, professional clubs, supporters and community activity

Simon Oldham, Managing Director of Highland SpringGroup, said, “Highland Spring and Scottish Rugby are two Scottish icons, perfectly matched through shared values and a passion for helping people perform at their best. Over the past two years, we’ve built an authentic and highly collaborative relationship – and this extension marks a bold next chapter

“Healthy hydration is essential to performance on and off the pitch. Our increased investment will help us take that message to even more people while continuing to hydrate Scotland’s players and supporters.”

Olaf Gueldner, Chief Customer Officer at Scottish Rugby, said, “The commitment from Saltire Energy to Scottish Rugby over the duration of the partnership is testament to the many shared values between our organisations. We are both passionate about supporting the game at grassroots level through our community clubs and schools.

Mike Loggie, CEO of Saltire Energy, said, “Saltire Energy is proud to continue our official partnership with Scottish Rugby. As we celebrate our 40th year in business, our partnership with SRU reinforces our commitment to the communities we operate in and our dedication to the role sport plays in young people’s lives.”

title: Anytime Fitness Australia Named Official Gym Partner of West Coast Eagles
article_text:
Anytime Fitness Australia has signed a two-year commercial agreement to become the Official Gym Partner of the West Coast Eagles, spanning both the club’s Australian Football League (AFL) and AFL Women’s (AFLW) programmes.

The partnership connects the national fitness franchise network, comprising more than 647 clubs and 800,000 members nationwide, directly with the Eagles’ record-breaking supporter base of 115,324 financial members across Western Australia.

By linking Anytime Fitness’s club footprint across Greater Perth, the Peel region, and regional Western Australia with the Eagles’ elite men’s and women’s squads, the deal aims to bridge high-performance sport with everyday community health.

The agreement follows Anytime Fitness’s recent major activation in Perth as the Official Gym Partner of ExPRO, Australia’s fitness, wellness, and lifestyle festival, further consolidating the brand’s commercial and recruitment expansion along the Western Australian coastline.

Anytime Fitness Australia Managing Director, Simon Thompson, highlighted the value of aligning with Western Australia’s largest sporting institution to drive grassroots fitness participation.

“The West Coast Eagles unite generations of West Australians, with a loyalty and pride that reaches far beyond the football field.”

“Our ambition is to give more people across WA a welcoming place to train, build strength and feel their best.

“Becoming the Official Gym Partner of the Eagles’ AFL and AFLW teams builds on that commitment, bringing together two organisations that share a passion for sport, fitness and the positive role they play in people’s lives,” Thompson said.

West Coast Eagles CEO, Don Pyke, underscored the natural synergy between elite athletic performance and accessible community wellbeing.

“We’re proud to welcome Anytime Fitness to the West Coast Eagles and look forward to building a strong partnership across our AFL and AFLW programs.”

“Both organisations understand the important role sport and physical activity can play in bringing people together and supporting their health and wellbeing.

“We’re excited to work together to encourage more people in our community to get active and enjoy the benefits of an active lifestyle,” Pyke said.

title: How the Sphere became the heart of the Las Vegas Grand Prix
article_text:
It's eye-catching, spectacular and unmistakably Las Vegas. The Sphere has become an integral part of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, and we explore how and why.

From giant driver portraits to live onboard footage and race updates, the Sphere has become one of the defining sights of the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Having opened just weeks before Formula 1 returned to the city in 2023, the enormous entertainment venue quickly became part of the race's identity, with its illuminated exterior providing a spectacular backdrop to the action.

But the Sphere is far more than a giant advertising screen. With its ability to display everything from yellow flags to live footage, its become a staple of the race with increasingly creative ways to showcase information.

The Sphere opened on September 29, 2023, with Irish rock band U2 beginning a 40-show residency at the venue. Its distinctive design and enormous LED exterior immediately made it one of Las Vegas' most recognisable landmarks.

Made up of 54,000 metres squared of LED displays on its exterior, it is the largest video screen in the world, and inside, an audience of up to 20,000 people are treated to a 16K resolution wraparound interior LED screen.

Formula 1 returned to Las Vegas on November 18, 2023, more than four decades after the city hosted the Caesars Palace Grand Prix in 1981 and 1982. With the Sphere sitting alongside the new circuit, it quickly became part of the event's identity, entertaining fans while providing live updates from the track.

Right from the off, the Sphere would sync with the FIA’s circuit calls, displaying a huge yellow flag and a wrap-around Safety Car message, or a rippling red flag if the session had come to a stop.

Orbi, the giant yellow emoji face displayed on the Sphere, even donned a racing helmet and appeared to watch the cars as they exited Turn 9. Driver profiles were also on a loop, helping educate fans about what the drivers looked like outside of the cockpit and which teams they drove for.

And since then, the use of the huge display that measures 112m high and 157m wide has got ever more creative. Onboards were a frequent feature during the 2025 event, showing the cars lapping this rapid 6.201km track layout.

"The Sphere has become a great partner, and so we have a lot of advanced conversations and meetings to organise the different types of content,” Austin Brown, VP of Marketing at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, explains.

"We have the partnerships content as well as chequered flags, yellow and red flags, and then we have some podium celebrations, so it's a combination of F1's broadcast team cueing content in real time with the Sphere team who are on site for the duration of the week.

"We actually pull some of the telemetry data from the feed that goes over to the Sphere team, so that we can track things like fastest lap; depending on how the race results end up, we can post that content live to Sphere. So we pre-build a lot of the content that's driver- or team related, and some of these moments that we know might occur on track, and then we feed that data or the broadcast team cues live content to align with track activity for broadcast, socials or the on-site experience with fans in attendance.”

The Las Vegas Grand Prix has proved to be the pinnacle of F1’s entertainment ecosystem, with continuous celebrity spotting, big shows and performances across the race weekend, and definitely follows the saying “everything is bigger in Vegas”. For the race organisers, the Sphere was going to be no exception.

“Las Vegas' role on the F1 calendar is to push the sports and entertainment landscape,” Brown says, describing the Sphere as “an iconic canvas” that is “a massive win for everybody involved".

As a Las Vegas native, Brown loves to see the tourist attractions showcased on the Sphere, and adds that the vibrancy of its neon colours fits a night race very well.

"To see a lot of the F1 drivers at that scale on Sphere is just a really fun opportunity. We've pre-filmed content with drivers in the past where they're taking different actions on the Sphere; there's an opportunity for animated and still graphics up there. To see Lewis Hamilton at the scale of Sphere is just a really special moment to deliver to fans. We're excited to see what kind of content is produced and live this year.”

Inside the Sphere, the schedule is packed. After this year’s Las Vegas Grand Prix, Backstreet Boys will be performing the Official Afterparty at Sphere. They’re one of several groups and artists who have had residencies at the unique venue, with others including the likes of Metallica and No Doubt, and more are scheduled throughout 2027, with John Mayer and P!nk both booked in.

As well as pop royalty, there are also many immersive shows to watch inside such as The Wizard of Oz which comes with 4D effects. The grand space of the venue, which can fit the entire Statue of Liberty inside, has 17,385 seats and uses Stereographic Projection and custom cameras to capture the ultra-wide videos and images that you see on the wraparound screens.

“I think when Liberty Media acquired the sport, and then F1 was looking at new markets back in 2022, that is when they really started to explore Vegas as a market,” Brown concludes. “I think it was really trying to find a platform to continue to grow the sport to a lot of untapped fans in the US. So where better to do that than in the sports and entertainment capital of the world with a night race that just shows off everything the city has to offer?

title: Aussie Broadband Renews Western Sydney Wanderers FC Partnership for 2026/27 A-League Season
article_text:
Australian telecommunications provider Aussie Broadband has extended its partnership with the Western Sydney Wanderers FC for the 2026/27 season. Building upon a successful two-year commercial partnership, the renewal confirms Aussie Broadband will continue as the club’s Official Telecommunications Partner, Official Grassroots Football Partner, and Senior Partner. The agreement reinforces corporate investment across both elite match-day operations at CommBank Stadium and regional community engagement across Western Sydney.

Under the renewed terms, Aussie Broadband maintains naming and supporting rights across key community and volunteer properties, including the Wander Crew match-day volunteer programme, the Club Ambassador Program, and the Community Champions initiative. A central activation pillar of the agreement remains the annual Grassroots Recognition Round, which spotlights local clubs, administrators, and volunteers driving football participation growth throughout Western Sydney.

Aussie Broadband group chief financial officer, Darren Rowland, emphasised the alignment between the telecommunications operator’s local-first business model and the Wanderers’ regional community footprint.

“We’re thrilled to continue our partnership with Western Sydney Wanderers FC for this year’s A-League season.

“Aussie Broadband was built on a commitment to supporting local communities, and that remains a core part of who we are today.

“The Wanderers share that same community-first mindset, making this a natural partnership.

“We hope our support helps the club build on their positive impact across Western Sydney, bringing people together and strengthening connections throughout the community,” Rowland said.

Western Sydney Wanderers CEO, Scott Hudson, highlighted the commercial and social value of partnering with an organisation invested in volunteer and grassroots recognition.

“We’re incredibly proud to be continuing our partnership with Aussie Broadband, an organisation that genuinely understands the value of community and the importance of supporting the people who make football what it is.”

“From our Wander Crew volunteers who give so much of their time on match days, to the grassroots clubs and individuals working tirelessly to grow the game across Western Sydney, this partnership is about recognising the people who are so often the unsung heroes of our sport.

“What has made this relationship so meaningful is Aussie Broadband’s willingness to invest in initiatives that create genuine connections and make a positive difference beyond the football pitch.

“We’re delighted to have their continued support for the 2026/27 season and look forward to building on the foundations we’ve established together,” Hudson said.

title: Premier League gambling advertising ban falls short of full compliance
article_text:
The English Premier League has moved away from bookmaker logos on the front of playing shirts from the 2026/27 season. However, gambling advertising has not disappeared from broadcast coverage. Research from the University of Bristol found that the measure reduced the overall volume of advertising messages by only around 10%, with approximately half of that reduction offset by increased exposure on sleeves, training kits, and pitchside LED boards.

The viewing experience has changed only minimally in practice. Thousands of betting brand references continue to accompany every match, casting doubt on the real effectiveness of the voluntary restriction and fuelling debate about the need for stricter regulation.

Modern gambling entertainment, which includes sports betting, is growing more popular every year. This covers everything from slots and poker to live shows with real dealers. According to data available here, Monopoly Live by Evolution and similar games have become genuine hits over the past several months.

The popularity of these products is linked to the fact that British audiences have a fondness for enjoying live game shows, and not only gambling formats. The iGaming industry in the country therefore strives to match local tastes, which helps it remain successful. Sports betting, naturally, is also a long-standing British tradition, which is why its advertising continues despite resistance from authorities.

The ban is narrowly constructed and applies exclusively to the front of playing shirts. All other space has remained open to bookmakers. The following formats are permitted:

A source who had worked on commercial contracts between betting operators and clubs explained to Front Office Sports that for a global audience “the front of the shirt is prestigious, but LED boards matter most for those watching matches around the world.” It is the constant visibility of pitchside advertising that delivers maximum reach, rather than a static logo on a player’s chest.

Betting operators’ interest in English football is driven by direct conversion. Sean Connell, editor of industry consultancy The Sponsor, notes that “bookmakers need enormous volumes of brand awareness,” and club sponsorship creates “a fairly direct link between the logo on the shirt and the number of newly registered customers.” The male Premier League audience aligns with the core target demographic of betting operators, and no better vehicle for this category simply exists.

The pioneer was Betfair, which signed a deal with Fulham in 2002. Within a decade, three-quarters of Premier League clubs were carrying bookmaker logos. According to a source close to several deals, betting operators paid roughly twice as much as rivals from other industries, and this generosity created a deep financial dependency on the category among clubs.

Political pressure built gradually. In 2020, a House of Lords committee described the regulation of the gambling industry as “soft” and recommended a complete ban on sports sponsorship by bookmakers. The Premier League adopted a pre-emptive approach and in 2023 announced a voluntary phased withdrawal of bookmaker logos from the front of shirts, with a three-year transition period. The government, in turn, signalled that it would not tighten shirt rules if the league managed the process itself.

Half of Premier League clubs had to find new front-of-shirt sponsors last summer. Bournemouth expanded its agreement with insurance company Vitality, Brentford added a playing shirt to its contract with recruitment platform Indeed, and Nottingham Forest signed a last-minute deal with financial firm Marex. Sunderland and Chelsea began the season without a front-of-shirt sponsor at all, though Chelsea subsequently signed a contract with crypto company Circle.

According to estimates by Ampere Analytics analyst Adam Lewis, the eight clubs that changed partners grew the combined annual value of their front-of-shirt contracts from $89m (£67m) to $99m (£75m). At the same time, the combined value of sleeve and training kit deals rose from $176m (£133m) to $206m (£156m), with a significant portion of bookmaker money migrating into these permitted areas. The bookmakers’ share of training kit sponsorships is estimated to have exceeded 50%.

The ban applies only at Premier League level. Clubs in the three lower divisions retain the right to sign deals with betting operators, and the government concluded that a full ban risked devastating the finances of dozens of clubs. In addition, bookmaker brands are visible in UEFA competitions held at English grounds. Betano, the former sponsor of Aston Villa, is the lead partner of the Europa League, the Conference League, and the upcoming Euro 2028 in the United Kingdom and Ireland.

Against the backdrop of restrictions on traditional bookmakers, attention is shifting to prediction markets, which could potentially attempt to circumvent the definition of “gambling.” The leading platforms Polymarket and Kalshi do not yet operate legally in the United Kingdom, but the Premier League’s global reach makes sponsorship attractive for promotion in overseas markets. The Premier League stated that it “cannot comment on whether prediction market operators would fall under the existing rule.” The Gambling Commission is more sceptical, taking the view that such an operator would be unlikely to classify itself as a “non-gambling” product on UK territory.

A European precedent has already been set. An Italian court this summer struck down Polymarket’s $21m (€19m) contract with Lazio, ruling that such platforms fall under the gambling sponsorship ban. In England, regulation is softer thanks to the league’s self-regulatory approach, and the question remains open. The decisive moment will come with the first real contract and the regulator’s response.

title: Christian Horner Drops Major Hint on Alpine Formula 1 Team Stake
article_text:
Christian Horner has dropped a major hint about a potential return to F1, suggesting that he would only consider investing his efforts in a team if he had the authority to influence meaningful change. Horner has been linked with a possible investment in Alpine, with minority shareholder Otro Capital reportedly exploring a sale of its 24% stake in the team.

During an interview with Vincenzo Landino, the former Red Bull boss shed light on the possibility of purchasing the minority stake in Alpine.

"What is the point in buying a minority stake if you can't influence change? There's no point investing in a team that you can't drive change into. So for me that would be nonsensical to do something like that," Horner said [5:10]

Horner was sacked from his role as CEO and Team Principal of Red Bull Racing on July 9, 2025. His sudden exit marked the end of his 20-year tenure with the Milton Keynes-based team.

Despite being linked with several potential opportunities, Horner, who had secured multiple drivers' and constructors' championships for Red Bull, has indicated that he is in no rush to return to the F1 paddock.

"I'd only want to go back if, you know, first of all I had equity in a project and secondly that I was in a position to enable change. I won pretty much a third of the races that I ever competed in," Horner said.

The Briton also pointed to his achievements at Red Bull as evidence of what he could accomplish with the right resources and commitment.

"I don't want to go back just to take part. I'm not afraid of taking on a project, and certainly you know my time at Red Bull demonstrated that if you have a desire and a commitment you can achieve anything – whether it's with a chassis or even obviously laterally with the engine," he added.

The former Red Bull team principal also acknowledged how dramatically Formula 1 team valuations have increased alongside the sport's commercial growth, particularly in the United States.

"Well, valuations of the teams are just going off the charts at the moment because of the success of Formula 1. You look at how the sport has grown, particularly in the US over the last few years. The franchises now have real value to them," Horner said.

"I mean, six/seven/eight years ago, half of the grid would have been pretty much insolvent. Now the smallest team in Formula 1 has at least a $2 billion valuation."

Otro Capital acquired a 24% minority stake in Alpine in 2023 and has reportedly appointed investment bank BDT & MSD Partners to explore a potential sale.

According to GPFans, the stake is now estimated to be worth approximately $787 million, based on a reported total team valuation of $3.28 billion (a 58 percent increase on 2025).

title: John Terry and Kevin Durant back MWS growth
article_text:
MWS has secured £15.5m in new investment from a group of sports investors led by Gamma Waves Partners & John Terry to support its international expansion

The investment in MWS, previously known as MatchWornShirt, includes backing from former England and Chelsea captain John Terry and NBA player Kevin Durant through 35V, his investment company with Rich Kleiman.

Gamma Waves Partners is the lead investor in the round. The sports and technology investment platform was Co-Founded by former Italy international Giorgio Chiellini, former Juventus chairman Andrea Agnelli and Rocco Benetton.

Other investors include Pacers Sports & Entertainment, the ownership group behind the Indiana Pacers and Indiana Fever, and Joyned Capital, whose members include Arsenal player Jurriën Timber and his brother Quinten Timber. Tottenham Hotspur defender Tosin Adarabioyo has also invested individually.

The funding will support the sports memorabilia platform’s expansion, including further growth in North America. MWS has established partnerships across football and has expanded into sports including basketball, ice hockey, rugby and cycling.

Founded in Amsterdam in 2017 by brothers Tijmen Zonderwijk and Bob Zonderwijk, MWS operates an online auction platform for authenticated match-worn sports memorabilia. Its partnership portfolio includes more than 450 clubs globally, with Chelsea among its UK football partners.

Tijmen Zonderwijk, Co-Founder and CEO of MWS, said, “The scale of the names and businesses involved in this group of investors demonstrates a collective passion for what we have already built here at MWS, and for that, we’re incredibly proud. It also represents a shared vision for the future, and we’re excited to accelerate the growth of the business whilst remaining true to our values.

“All involved across this group of investors have core experience in the world of sport and entertainment, but more widely than that, building businesses that sit at the intersection of sport, culture, commerce and community. This is where it becomes an even more exciting prospect; building on a shared vision to bring fans and collectors around the world closer to the moments and the icons that are central to their sporting passions.”

Perfect Game China Launch Names JinMu Sports as Exclusive Country Partner
article_text:
- Perfect Game cites 300 million children among China’s 1.4 billion people as the opportunity behind its first China operation.

- JinMu Sports, led by former Triple-A player and ex-MLB China baseball operations head Ray Chang, is the exclusive Country Partner.

- Events open with a pan-Asia Showcase in January 2027, then expand across four provinces plus Shanghai and Beijing.

- Chinese athletes gain Player Profiles, scouting data and pathways into select Perfect Game events in the United States.

Perfect Game, the Sanford, Florida-based youth baseball and softball platform and scouting service, is expanding into China through its new Global Country Partner Program, the company announced on November 17, 2026. Perfect Game selected JinMu Sports, led by former professional player Ray Chang, as its exclusive Country Partner in China. A pan-Asia Showcase in January 2027 will open the Perfect Game China schedule.

Perfect Game pointed to the size of the market in its announcement: China has 1.4 billion people, including 300 million children, according to the company.

The China launch runs through the Global Country Partner Program, which Perfect Game described as part of its international growth strategy to give young athletes more chances to compete, develop and gain exposure through its events, scouting and media platform. Rather than operating directly, Perfect Game is working through a local partner, and JinMu is one of the program’s founding Country Partners, per Kash Shaikh, Perfect Game’s Chief Marketing Officer and Head of International.

“China has all the ingredients to build a robust youth baseball ecosystem, with talented players, strong infrastructure, and a culture built on sportsmanship and competition,” Shaikh said.

Who Is Ray Chang, the Founder of JinMu Sports?

Chang, a Chinese American, spent more than a decade playing professionally in the United States and reached Triple-A in the San Diego Padres, Pittsburgh Pirates, Boston Red Sox, Minnesota Twins and Cincinnati Reds organizations, according to the release. He represented China in four World Baseball Classics, in 2009, 2013, 2017 and 2023, and helped deliver the country’s first-ever World Baseball Classic victory in 2009.

Chang took over baseball operations for MLB China in 2017, Perfect Game said. He also has a history with the company as a player, saying he competed in Perfect Game tournaments more than 20 years ago.

“This partnership represents an important opportunity for Chinese players, teams and families to access new levels of competition and development international exposure, including playing at the collegiate level,” Chang said.

Perfect Game China plans a series of tournaments, showcases and player development opportunities, beginning with the pan-Asia Showcase in January 2027, the company said. Initial events will take place across Jiangsu, Guangdong, Fujian and Sichuan provinces, with tournaments scheduled in Shanghai, Beijing and additional cities.

Perfect Game said all Chinese athletes will have access to Perfect Game Player Profiles, scouting data and event statistics, giving them greater visibility with college recruiters and professional scouts.

A Route From Chinese Showcases to U.S. Draft Scouting

The partnership will also establish pathways for top Chinese players and teams to compete in select Perfect Game events in the United States and in future international competitions, according to the release. Those U.S. events carry weight with MLB clubs: Perfect Game says 92 percent of players selected in the 2025 MLB Draft had played in its events, and more than 2,600 Perfect Game alumni have played in Major League Baseball.

China has competed in every World Baseball Classic since the tournament’s inception in 2006, Perfect Game noted. The release does not say which U.S. events Chinese teams will enter or how many players will qualify, the details that will decide how wide that pathway opens in 2027.

Source / Adapted From: Perfect Game Press Release, November 17, 2026, perfectgame.org

title: F1 Academy prepares for Las Vegas with special livery
article_text:
F1 Academy teams and drivers have begun unveiling their special liveries for the Las Vegas GP as they aim to make it a weekend to remember under the lights.

Alisha Palmowski already wrapped up the F1 Academy championship by taking the title in Austin after a stellar season. However, with the final race weekend to go, the series still puts its best foot forward as several teams head into Las Vegas with stylish liveries.

The newly crowned champion arrives in Vegas in a special championship livery, created in collaboration with Visa. The Red Bull Racing Academy driver will have a golden chrome finish on every partner logo and her racing number, 21, standing out against the stunning electric blue inspired by Visa. Under the lights in Sin City, the livery includes a light-reactive metallic finish for Palmowski. Additionally, the driver will be fitted with a special race suit with the electric blue design.

“I’m so excited to race in Las Vegas with this special championship livery! Visa and the Team have created something really special to celebrate my achievement, and I’m incredibly grateful to have that recognition on track for my final race in F1 ACADEMY. Although I’ve already secured the title, winning is always the goal, and it would be amazing to finish the season with a victory in this car!”

Another team that arrives in Vegas with a new look is Alpine. The F1 team has Franco Colapinto and Pierre Gasly showing off the iconic pink colour on the A526’s sidepod. In the same vein, Alpine-supported F1 Academy driver Nina Gademan will sport the stunning Alpine colours.

title: High Match Tempo Linked to Greater Sponsorship Visibility in Broadcast Study
article_text:
A comparative computer vision analysis of European cup soccer broadcasts found that sponsorship visibility reached significantly higher levels during matches characterized by high in-game action and tempo. In an observational investigation published in BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation, researchers recorded a peak sponsorship visibility performance index score of 1,446 points during a high-action intensity match, whereas the maximum efficiency score recorded during a lower-tempo, highly controlled fixture was 23.93 percent lower. The findings demonstrate that brand visibility in digital sports broadcasting is strongly tied to immediate match dynamics rather than overall broadcast length alone.

The team sought to investigate the relational associations connecting dynamic game content to sponsorship efficiency within digital broadcasting environments. Using an exploratory, comparative framework across two distinct European cup fixtures, the authors evaluated how shifting phases of live gameplay and production choices influence commercial exposure on digital streaming platforms.

To conduct their investigation, the authors adopted a computational content analysis methodology paired with a comparative multiple case study design. The dataset comprised official match recordings of two high-profile European cup games streamed on the YouTube platform in late April 2026: Paris Saint-Germain FC against Bayern Munich on April 28, 2026, and Atlético Madrid against Arsenal FC on April 29, 2026.

The research team tracked sponsorship visibility on a per-second basis using a custom artificial intelligence-driven computer vision algorithm developed specifically in the MATLAB computational environment. This algorithm integrated the Region of Interest technique to quantify three primary visual exposure parameters across the broadcast stream: in-screen brand density, temporal exposure duration, and spatial positioning metrics. This automated framework enabled a continuous, per-second measurement of sponsor placements throughout the entirety of both match recordings.

Across the two monitored broadcasts, the algorithm revealed that sponsorship visibility peaked during critical offensive sequences and goal-scoring moments, coinciding with heightened action and open-field play. Conversely, close-up camera angles and replay sequences were consistently associated with temporary drops in sponsor visibility. In the match defined by high-action intensity, the visibility index achieved its maximum score of 1,446 points, while the corresponding peak efficiency score observed in the controlled, lower-tempo contest lagged by 23.93 percent.

The observational data highlighted a strong relationship between television direction choices and brand exposure potential. Specific production decisions preferred by the broadcasting director, including the timing of close-up player framing, camera angle transitions, and slow-motion replays, exhibited strong associations with the screen persistence and visual exposure potential of visible brand assets.

The authors concluded that sponsorship performance in digital sports broadcasting is relationally associated not only with total cumulative exposure duration, but critically with the instantaneous content flow of the match and real-time broadcasting production dynamics. Furthermore, the researchers emphasized that automated artificial intelligence and computer vision analysis methods offer objective, quantifiable, and data-driven evaluation tools for sports marketing research, providing distinct evaluative capabilities relative to traditional, non-automated methodologies.

Article References: Bingöl, Ş., Öner, İ., Aksu, A., Tanoğlu, G., Türkay, H., Polat, S., & Erdoğan, R. (2026). Content dynamics and their impact on sponsorship efficiency in digital sports broadcasting: a comparative visual exposure analysis via PSG–Bayern Munich and Atletico Madrid–Arsenal matches. BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13102-026-02227-1

News Source: Ophelia Keating. (November 18, 2026). High Match Tempo Linked to Greater Sponsorship Visibility in Broadcast Study. Scienmag.
